# Minimum line-height baselines

Original controls generated by `tools/minimum_line_baseline_fixture.py`, using
the original column-boundary package scaffold. Each committed DOCX was opened
read-only in the reference application and exported to its corresponding PDF.
References retain source/PDF SHA-256 hashes and independent pypdf text positions.
No corpus text, embedded fonts or third-party engine is included.

Eighteen three-line controls combine Arial, Calibri and Times New Roman at
10/16 pt with minimum heights of 6/18/24 pt. Six single-line controls compare
automatic and 12 pt minimum spacing with 10/11/12 pt paragraph marks.
These establish bottom alignment in expanded minimum lines, natural expansion
for undersized minimums, and unchanged automatic metrics. Larger end marks do
not enlarge these nonempty text lines.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33 (printed page 250) instead requires centering when
an exact/minimum line has spare height. The reference application's minimum-line behavior is an
observed divergence. The engine follows the reference application without changing stored spacing.
The browser oracle retains the 0.15 pt tolerance, requiring each native font
for its baseline comparison, and checks editing, undo and export/reopen.
This is a text-position comparison, not a pixel-identity claim.
